title: Béchamel Sauce
subtitle: Classic French white sauce
excerpt: A smooth, creamy sauce made from butter, flour, and hot milk, seasoned with nutmeg and bay leaf. The foundation of lasagne, moussaka, croque monsieur, and cauliflower cheese.

recipe.sourceNotes: Béchamel is one of the five French mother sauces. The name comes from Louis de Béchamel, a steward at the court of Louis XIV, though the sauce predates him under different names. It is a roux-based sauce: equal weights of butter and flour are cooked together first to form a roux, which is then gradually combined with hot milk to produce a lump-free, thickened sauce. The roux must be cooked for at least 2 minutes before adding the milk, or the sauce will taste of raw flour. The milk is infused with a bay leaf and nutmeg before adding for extra depth. The consistency can be adjusted by using more or less milk: a thick béchamel for lasagne, a thinner one for pouring over vegetables.

content.text: Heat the milk before adding it to the roux: cold milk added to a hot roux is one of the main causes of lumps. Add the milk gradually at first, whisking constantly after each addition until smooth before adding more. Once all the milk is incorporated, switch to a wooden spoon or silicone spatula and stir over medium-low heat until the sauce thickens and no longer tastes of flour. Season generously: under-seasoned béchamel is bland.
Warm the milk in a separate pan with the bay leaf until steaming but not boiling. Remove the bay leaf.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir to combine. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes. The roux will turn slightly golden and smell biscuity.
Remove from the heat. Add a ladleful of warm milk and whisk vigorously until smooth. Return to medium heat. Add the remaining milk in three or four additions, whisking well after each one.

Stir continuously over medium-low heat for 5 to 8 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Use immediately, or press cling film directly onto the surface to prevent a skin forming.
